content.value_statement: Durable TypeScript services need clear workflow rules and failure handling. This skill guides DBOS workflows, steps, queues, clients, communication, testing, and upgrades.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to configure and launch DBOS TypeScript applications before running workflows.
Shows workflow and step rules for durable execution and recovery after failures.
Covers queues, concurrency, partitioning, deduplication, priorities, and rate limits.
Documents DBOS communication patterns, including events, messages, and streaming.
Guides DBOSClient usage, background workflows, testing setup, versioning, and patching.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not a runnable DBOS application template.
Examples use placeholder services and must be adapted to the user application.
It does not verify the installed DBOS SDK version at runtime.
It does not replace production security review for databases, APIs, or credentials.

use_cases.title: Create a Durable Service
use_cases.description: Plan workflows, steps, and DBOS launch order for a new TypeScript backend.

use_cases.title: Tune Queue Processing
use_cases.description: Select queue settings for concurrency, partitioning, deduplication, priorities, and rate limits.

use_cases.title: Test Workflow Behavior
use_cases.description: Set up unit and integration tests for DBOS workflows with clear lifecycle handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a DBOS App
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a DBOS TypeScript application. Identify the workflows, steps, launch setup, and configuration I need.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Async Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate migration from ordinary async functions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript workflow design and tell me which operations should become DBOS steps, transactions, or queues.

prompt_templates.title: Design Queue Workers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DBOS queue strategy for mixed CPU and GPU workers with concurrency limits, priorities, and retry behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Recovery Semantics
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my DBOS TypeScript architecture for determinism, idempotency, workflow versioning, patching, and recovery risks.

output_examples.input: A user asks where to place a third-party API call in a workflow.
output_examples.output: The skill explains that external I/O belongs in a DBOS step and describes how this supports durable replay.

output_examples.input: A user needs separate CPU and GPU workers for queued jobs.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines queue listening, worker configuration, and safe enqueue behavior for heterogeneous worker pools.

output_examples.input: A user wants to test DBOS workflows consistently.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends unit mocks, integration database isolation, DBOS shutdown, and launch ordering checks.

best_practices: Configure and launch DBOS before starting workflows or accepting application traffic.
Put non-deterministic work, external calls, and database writes inside durable steps or transactions.
Use queues and workflow IDs intentionally to control concurrency, deduplication, and idempotency.
anti_patterns: Running external API calls directly inside workflow logic without a DBOS step.
Starting workflows from inside steps instead of using workflow or queue APIs from the right layer.
Changing workflow behavior without considering versioning, patching, or deterministic replay.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users design and review DBOS TypeScript applications that use durable workflows, steps, queues, and clients.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete application?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples that users adapt to their own TypeScript application.

faq.question: Can it help with DBOS queues?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers queue basics, concurrency, deduplication, listening, partitioning, priority, and rate limiting.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains unit testing with mocks and integration testing with a Postgres-backed DBOS setup.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. It shows environment variable configuration examples, but users must manage secrets and database credentials securely.
